sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Floyd County, KY?
sections.html:
Two offices split the job. The Floyd County Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets what each parcel is worth, and the Floyd County Sheriff's tax division mails and collects the bills. Neither office picks the rate that gets applied to the value.

The PVA works from 149 S. Central Ave., Room 5, in Prestonsburg, and answers at (606) 886-9622. Its own website says the office appraises real and personal property at 100 percent of fair market value and does not calculate or collect taxes. The sheriff's tax division shares the street address, takes mail at P.O. Box 152, and can be reached at (606) 886-8965 on weekdays between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

sections.h2: What is Floyd County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Floyd County sits in the mountains of eastern Kentucky and covers 393 square miles of land. The legislature created it in 1799 from parts of Fleming, Montgomery and Mason counties, effective June 1, 1800, and Prestonsburg is the seat. The other cities are Allen, Martin, Wayland and Wheelwright, and about 78 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census.

Coal shaped the housing stock. The first commercial coal mine in eastern Kentucky opened in 1900 at Betsy Layne, and company towns such as Wheelwright, Wayland, Garrett, Emma and Bypro followed. The county peaked above 53,000 residents in 1950 and counted 35,942 in 2020. The Floyd County School District runs the public schools.

Federal figures show how modest the local market is:

  • Estimated population in 2025: 34,401, a 4.3 percent drop from the April 2020 base.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $98,700.
  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 72.2 percent.
  • Median gross rent: $672 a month.
  • Median household income: $41,279, with 27.7 percent of people in poverty.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 2.

With so little new construction, almost every sale is an older house, and many carry repair needs. A tax balance of a few thousand dollars takes a much bigger bite out of a $98,700 house than out of a Frankfort or Lexington-area home.

sections.h2: When are Floyd County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills are due by December 31 of the assessment year, and the schedule is set in KRS 134.015. Paying everything by November 1 takes 2 percent off. Between November 2 and December 31 you pay the printed amount. A 5 percent penalty applies to January payments, and 10 percent applies once January is over.

The Floyd County Sheriff's site announced that 2026 bills became payable on October 1 and offers an online payment option. If a mortgage company escrows your taxes, it normally pays the sheriff for you, so confirm with the servicer that the bill reached it.

The tax is also a personal debt of whoever owned the property on the assessment date, which is January 1. A buyer who closes in March therefore usually does not own the previous year's bill, but the seller and buyer should still agree in the contract about who pays what, since an unpaid bill can follow the parcel.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Floyd County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA, because Kentucky requires a conference before any formal appeal. The tax roll is open to inspection for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and conferences can begin as soon as assessment notices go out.

  • Sit down with the PVA or a deputy, who must explain how your value was reached and write up the meeting.
  • File the appeal with the county clerk by the close of business on the workday after the inspection period ends.
  • Prepare evidence such as photos, repair estimates, insurance records, construction costs and nearby sale listings. A board denies an appeal that comes without documentation.
  • Appear when the local board of assessment appeals meets, between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes. Skipping the hearing ends your right to continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Anyone you pay to speak for you must fit a short list of professions set by KRS 133.120, such as an attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, and must bring written authorization from you.

sections.h2: Does Floyd County have a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can have $49,100 taken off the assessed value of their home for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The Floyd County PVA's website says a formal application is required before any exemption is granted, and that the disability version covers people who are 100 percent disabled.

On a house assessed at the county median of $98,700, the taxable amount drops to $49,600. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability applicants need to have been classified as totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program and must file again each year unless they are a veteran with a service-connected disability or have been found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Floyd County house with property tax unpaid?
sections.html:
The debt does not disappear at closing. KRS 134.015 keeps a delinquency lien attached to the parcel no matter who owns it, so a title search will turn it up and the buyer's lender will want it cleared.

The Department of Revenue describes what follows a missed April 15 deadline. The sheriff hands unpaid bills to the county clerk, who records a lien and starts adding 1 percent interest for every month. The county attorney then mails a 30-day notice and, if needed, a second one, and a clerk's tax sale can be held 90 to 135 days after the transfer. In a normal-schedule county that window runs from about July 14 to August 28.

  • Ask the sheriff's tax division at (606) 886-8965 for the exact amount due before you list.
  • Settle the balance from your sale proceeds at closing, or pay it earlier to keep clerk and county attorney commissions off the bill.
  • If the house needs work and back taxes are piling up, a buyer who purchases as-is and closes on a short timeline can take over both problems in one deal.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Floyd County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Floyd County Sheriff's tax division at 149 S Central Ave. in Prestonsburg, by mail to P.O. Box 152, or through the online option on the sheriff's website. The tax division's number is (606) 886-8965.

faqs.q: Does the PVA collect taxes or set the rate in Floyd County?
faqs.a: No. The PVA's website states that the office does not determine tax rates, calculate taxes or collect them. It values property and handles exemption applications, and you reach it at (606) 886-9622.

faqs.q: What is the last day to get the 2 percent discount in Floyd County?
faqs.a: November 1 of the assessment year. After that the bill is due at face value through December 31, then a 5 percent penalty applies for January and 10 percent afterward.

faqs.q: How much is the Floyd County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. It reduces the assessed value of a home owned by someone who is 65 or older or totally disabled, and the application goes to the Floyd County PVA.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Floyd County house before the tax bill is paid?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the amount owed is cleared at or before closing. Get a payoff figure from the sheriff's tax division, because the lien stays on the property after a sale if the bill is left unpaid.
